how is the U.S. government going to deal with cyber, how do we operationalize fixing things that need to be fixed? Because these models are coming one way or the other,” Michael said.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p data-v-a500cf4d="" class="font-text text-lg leading-[1.6] mt-5 md:mt-[1.875rem]">But an array of <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/posts/conorgrennan_uh-boy-if-youre-wondering-how-politics-activity-7457153612645826560-HPCW?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAABVWAqEB_p3bQhDq_KcfRGtF4lCPUT7IUPQ" class="js-tealium-tracking" data-tracking="mpos=center&mid=ar_body&lindex=68&lcol="><u>tech executives</u></a>, industry-aligned <a href="https://x.com/neil_chilson/status/2052068397169688991?s=20" class="js-tealium-tracking" data-tracking="mpos=center&mid=ar_body&lindex=69&lcol="><u>policy groups</u></a> and former <a href="https://x.com/deanwball/status/2052058167803027631?s=20" class="js-tealium-tracking" data-tracking="mpos=center&mid=ar_body&lindex=70&lcol="><u>government officials</u></a> have raised concerns about the idea of the government mandating pre-release oversight of AI models, fearing it will hinder competition.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p data-v-a500cf4d="" class="font-text text-lg leading-[1.6] mt-5 md:mt-[1.875rem]">“If [approval is] something that can be withheld before going to market, that’s a huge issue for any company,” said Daniel Castro, president of Information Technology and Innovation Foundation — a think tank funded by companies such as Anthropic, Microsoft and Meta. “If one competitor got approval and the other didn’t, that could have a huge impact if we’re talking weeks or months in terms of their market access.”</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p data-v-a500cf4d="" class="font-text text-lg leading-[1.6] mt-5 md:mt-[1.875rem]">Voluntary federal evaluation and safety-testing agreements for new AI models have been in place for several years, with some tech companies submitting their models for scrutiny by the Commerce Department’s Center for AI Standards and Innovation. CAISI <a href="https://www.politico.com/news/2026/05/05/microsoft-xai-google-caisi-safety-testing-00906529" class="js-tealium-tracking" data-tracking="mpos=center&mid=ar_body&lindex=71&lcol="><u>this week announced</u></a> it had signed deals to conduct safety testing with other leading AI labs, including Google DeepMind, xAI, and Microsoft.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p data-v-a500cf4d="" class="font-text text-lg leading-[1.6] mt-5 md:mt-[1.875rem]">The Trump administration’s scramble to set new safety standards for AI models is being complicated by an ongoing spat between the Pentagon and Anthropic.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p data-v-a500cf4d="" class="font-text text-lg leading-[1.6] mt-5 md:mt-[1.875rem]">After Anthropic balked at letting the Pentagon use its models in autonomous lethal attacks and mass surveillance, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in March <a href="https://www.politico.com/news/2026/04/08/d-c-circuit-rejects-anthropic-plea-to-pause-supply-chain-risk-label-00864880" class="js-tealium-tracking" data-tracking="mpos=center&mid=ar_body&lindex=72&lcol="><u>designated the firm a supply chain risk</u></a> — an unprecedented move against a U.S. company that barred its model from use on DOD contracts. Trump separately <a href="https://www.politico.com/news/2026/02/27/trump-orders-all-federal-agencies-to-stop-using-anthropic-00804517" class="js-tealium-tracking" data-tracking="mpos=center&mid=ar_body&lindex=73&lcol="><u>gave federal agencies six months</u></a> to stop using Anthropic’s products, denouncing its executives as “leftwing nut jobs.”</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p data-v-a500cf4d="" class="font-text text-lg leading-[1.6] mt-5 md:mt-[1.875rem]">But federal agencies have been clamoring to get access to Mythos ever since Anthropic announced last month that it had built an AI system so effective at hacking that it could not be released to the general public.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p data-v-a500cf4d="" class="font-text text-lg leading-[1.6] mt-5 md:mt-[1.875rem]">Instead, it is exclusively sharing the model with a few dozen tech and security organizations, so they can get a head start on patching holes in critical software before malicious hackers exploit them. Anthropic has predicted that similar capabilities will be widely available within a year.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p data-v-a500cf4d="" class="font-text text-lg leading-[1.6] mt-5 md:mt-[1.875rem]">Anthropic’s archrival OpenAI <a href="https://www.politico.com/news/2026/05/07/openai-chatgpt-cyber-ai-model-00910704" class="js-tealium-tracking" data-tracking="mpos=center&mid=ar_body&lindex=74&lcol="><u>announced Thursday evening</u></a> that it is similarly allowing limited previews of a new AI tool, GPT-5.5-Cyber, that can find and patch cyber vulnerabilities.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p data-v-a500cf4d="" class="font-text text-lg leading-[1.6] mt-5 md:mt-[1.875rem]">Fear that the government could be caught off guard by another, more powerful model has prompted the Trump administration to take swift action, and marks a major shift for a president who vowed to slash AI regulation when he entered office.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p data-v-a500cf4d="" class="font-text text-lg leading-[1.6] mt-5 md:mt-[1.875rem]">Some in the industry are worried these actions could go too far.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p data-v-a500cf4d="" class="font-text text-lg leading-[1.6] mt-5 md:mt-[1.875rem]">“The argument’s always been that one of the reasons the U.S. is doing so well is that it’s taken a light-touch approach to this emerging technology that the government doesn’t necessarily know best,” said Castro with the Information Technology and Innovation Foundation. “I think there was a lot of surprise that that was even being considered.”</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></div><div
